head: working-tree
subject: HTTP/2 pseudo-header validation classifies each field name once
change: validateHeaderBlock called markRequestPseudo (up to five name comparisons) and then ran up to five more comparisons to capture the pseudo-header value, so one pseudo header cost six to ten comparisons. markRequestPseudo now returns the RequestPseudo tag, matching the existing HTTP/3 classifier, and the caller switches once to store the value. The response path drops the duplicate ':status' comparison and stores the value after markResponsePseudo succeeds. validateHeaderBlock is now public for callers that decode an HPACK block themselves, and bench-http2-hpack gained a header-validation scenario over a seven-field request block.
notes: The validation scenario uses the benchmark's seven-field request block (four pseudo headers plus three regular headers). The tag-based classifier is the same shape already used by HTTP/3, so the two runtimes now agree on pseudo-header classification. The encode-only 1.020x is code layout; HPACK decode and roundtrip scenarios are neutral within noise. benchmarks/baselines/http2-hpack.json was re-recorded with the new header-validation entry (nine entries, unpinned cpu32 fingerprint) so bench-gate keeps covering the existing HPACK scenarios. The host was loaded during the batch (load average roughly 5 to 15), so only interleaved ratios are claimed.
